text:
sam: @support getting reports that EU customers are hitting us in us-west and seeing high latency + intermittent 401s on /v1/generate. Example session id: sess_48a9. Anyone else?

mia: same. Dash shows spike in p50 latency from eu region at 2175009400 and a jump in auth failures. Top hits from edge-pop-ams-2.

steve: quick check — can someone run a dig/curl from an affected client to confirm DNS resolution and response headers? Look for X-Region / X-Edge headers.

jordan: ran a probe from an EU VM:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
34.201.12.45
$ curl -s -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health | grep -i "x-region"
X-Region: us-west-2
X-Edge: lhr-1
```
Routing to us-west-2 but edge says lhr-1 — inconsistent. Also saw: 401 response body: {"error":"auth_mismatch","detail":"token-region-mismatch"} for some tokens.

deploy-bot: geoip-sync-service failed to download new DB from s3 - status 503 at 2175009605 :geoip_sync:error

mia: that fits — stale geoip DB -> our routing layer maps IPs to wrong country/region causing fallback to different capacity pool. Also possible resolver caches at ISPs.

steve: can we get logs from geoip-sync? jordan can you paste the last 5 lines?

jordan: tail of sync log:
```
[2175009579] INFO: starting geoip sync
[2175009605] ERROR: s3.GetObject failed code=503 key=geoip/latest.mmdb
[2175009605] WARN: retrying in 30s
[2175009660] ERROR: s3.GetObject failed code=503
[2175009720] ERROR: sync failed after 3 retries
```

eng-infra: confirmed S3 returned 503 for the manifest fetch for region eu-west-1. We put a circuit breaker in the syncer — it fell back to the previous DB (which is 14 days old on ams nodes). That explains country->region mapping drift.

steve: mitigation steps: 1) force a geoip DB refresh from a healthy mirror 2) invalidate short-lived DNS/CDN cache for impacted pops 3) identify impacted customers for credits. Can infra run the forced refresh?

eng-infra: running: `/admin/geoip/force-refresh --source mirror-1 --pop ams-2`
(in progress)

monitoring-bot: geoip DB version on ams-2 was 2026-02-10, target is 2026-03-15.

jordan: after force-refresh (2175012000) did a fresh probe:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
3.249.67.21
$ curl -s -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health | grep -i "x-region"
X-Region: eu-west-1
X-Edge: ams-2
```
Responses now point to eu-west and 401 rate dropped. p50 latency trending back to baseline.

billing: please compile list of API keys with auth failures between 2175009000 and 2175013000. We'll prepare pro-rated credits for impacted customers.

sam: can we document repro steps for SEs so they can explain to customers? short checklist:
- confirm client IP -> geo lookup `curl https://ifconfig.co` + `geoiplookup`
- confirm `dig +short api.redwood.ai` and `curl -I` to check X-Region/X-Edge
- if routed to wrong region, escalate to eng-infra with probes + dig output

mia: adding note: ISP caches can hold stale mappings. For affected customers, ask them to flush DNS or try a different resolver (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) — but our forced refresh fixed most cases without customer action.

eng-infra: followups: 1) add exponential backoff + alerting on geoip sync 503s 2) add redundancy to mirrors 3) lower default DNS TTL for api.redwood.ai to 30s during rollouts 4) create automation to detect geoip DB drift vs resolver view.

billing: created ticket RED-3251 to list impacted accounts and proposed credits, will sync with ops.

monitoring-bot: p50 latency EU -> us-west reduced from 480ms to 82ms after 2175012100. auth failures down to baseline.

sam: closing loop — grateful for quick response. please post postmortem in #postmortems once root cause blameless write-up is ready. :thumbsup:
